All 5 vendors have replied. I limited the split to rows that are comparable, quoted and cleared the questionnaire. That leaves 15 of the 22 quote rows, and every SKU still has at least one eligible vendor. The cheapest cleared vendor per line is:
- V02 wins RM-001, 003, 004, 005 and 006.
- V03 wins RM-002 and RM-008.
- V01 wins RM-007.
- V04 wins RM-009 and RM-010.
Total spend is about Rs 10.28M. About Rs 7.86M of that (RM-009 and RM-010) sits with V04.

Clearing the questionnaire does not make these picks safe:
- V02's five lines all carry CLAIM_CONTRADICTED and WITHHELD flags. RM-003 also has COA_STALE, and RM-004 also has STRENGTH_ADJUSTED. V02's history is also weak: OTIF is 75–80% and defect rate is up to 6.6%.
- V04's two lines are late by 36 days. They also carry MOQ_COVER and SPACE_CLASH flags, and RM-009 has a COA_CONFLICT. V04 has no OTIF or defect history. That is missing data, not poor performance. A 36-day delay is a serious risk to the 20 December need-by date.
- V03's RM-008 has MOQ_COVER and STRENGTH_ADJUSTED flags. V03's RM-002 and V01's RM-007 have no flags, and both are early.

The cost-only split is cheap on paper, but I'd review the V02 and V04 lines before awarding them.
